page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.2xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized virtual server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with an identical count of 8 vCPUs operating at 2.8 GHz on AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 silicon, providing a single thread per core without simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources consist of 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per core ratio. Baseline network connectivity provides 17 Gbps bandwidth, while bundled local storage is absent and no discrete GPUs are provisioned.

Benchmark results show balanced compute behavior across general processing tasks, with notable strength in single-threaded decompression. In bzip3 decompression, the instance registers 14.48 GB/sec single-threaded, ranking in the top quartile of recorded test data, and delivers 109.93 GB/sec across multi-threaded execution. Synthetic CPU throughput is stable, yielding 13645.12 in multi-core stress-ng and 10105.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests. Static web serving reaches 19.31 GB/sec, accompanied by 17.88 million operations per second in Redis SET testing. Conversely, PassMark encryption achieves 1506.69, placing in the bottom quartile, and prompt processing for a 7B LLM model drops to 15.52 tokens per second due to the lack of hardware accelerators and restricted memory capacity.

From an infrastructure perspective, the c8gb.2xlarge delivers dedicated CPU execution suited for tasks where multi-threading contention must be eliminated. The lean 1:2 memory-to-core configuration emphasizes compute density over memory capacity, providing efficient resource utilization for build pipelines, CI/CD runners, containerized microservices, distributed caching, and web traffic proxying. Workloads requiring local high-speed scratch space, extensive database caches, or hardware-accelerated machine learning are constrained by the absence of local disks and GPUs.
description: Amazon Web Services c8gb.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the arm64 AWS Graviton ARMv9 architecture using Neoverse-V2 cores. Running on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores clocked at 2.8 GHz without multithreading, alongside 16.0 GB of system memory at 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides a 17 Gbps baseline network connection, lacks integrated local storage, and includes no discrete GPU hardware. Empirical testing reflects dependable multi-core execution and strong single-threaded decompression at 14.48 GB/sec in bzip3, coupled with consistent static web delivery and key-value database processing. It exhibits weaker metrics in cryptographic tests and medium-scale LLM prompt processing. With its dedicated core model and focused compute profile, c8gb.2xlarge is suited for CI/CD compilation, web serving, compression routines, and containerized microservices.
